title: Routine Antenatal Care: Booking Visit and Visit Schedule

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant woman at low risk attending a Saudi Ministry of Health primary health care centre: booking visit by 12 weeks, history, examination and booking tests, the eight-visit schedule (six in primary care and two in hospital), the three ultrasound scans, screening for gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, anaemia and infection, supplements, aspirin and anti-D prophylaxis, health education and when to move her to higher-risk care. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health antenatal page for the visit and scan schedule and NICE NG201 for the content of each visit, with medicine doses, administration and contraindications from product labels and NICE guidance.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-14.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The Saudi source is a Ministry of Health public patient-information page (updated 7 June 2023); the full Saudi Ministry of Health maternity care programme document was not found, so the criteria for eligibility for the basic care component (low risk) are not quoted.

NICE NG201 (England) sets booking by 10 weeks and fewer routine visits; the Saudi page sets booking before 12 weeks and eight visits. The Saudi schedule is used and the difference is shown in the comparison table.

Gestational diabetes screening: NICE refers to a separate guideline (NG3); the glucose thresholds in the investigations table (75 g test: fasting 5.1, 1 hour 10.0, 2 hours 8.5 mmol/L) are the widely used International Association of the Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups values and were not read from a Saudi source; confirm the local protocol.

Routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis: NICE TA156 describes two doses of 500 IU at 28 and 34 weeks or a single dose of 1,500 IU at 28 to 30 weeks, while the Rhophylac label gives a single 300 microgram (1,500 IU) dose at 28 to 30 weeks; the label regimen is written. The Saudi product and schedule used locally were not verified.
Aspirin 75 mg tablets are licensed for cardiovascular prevention, not for pre-eclampsia; the dose and timing come from NICE NG133 and the use is off-label (NICE NG133 states it must be prescribed).
Folic acid 400 microgram supplement doses come from NICE NG247 and have no pharmaceutical label in this topic; contraindication wording is from the 5 mg tablet label.

Vitamin D, iron, influenza, pertussis and COVID-19 vaccines in pregnancy, Rh prophylaxis after sensitising events and treatment of anaemia, gestational diabetes and hypertension are not written as regimens here.
Premarital screening results (haemoglobinopathies, infections) are mentioned in the Ministry of Health portal menu but their use in antenatal care was not verified.
Normal values for blood tests and blood pressure are standard adult pregnancy reference values; laboratories differ.
Differentials follow standard clinical practice and were not drawn from one source section.
Figures were read through automated extraction of web pages and label text; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Antenatal care detects problems that cause harm to mother and baby when found late, mainly pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, anaemia, infection and poor fetal growth, so that treatment or a change of care place can start early (NICE NG201, Section 1.2 Routine antenatal clinical care). The Saudi Ministry of Health schedule sets eight timed visits, six in primary care and two in hospital after transfer at 36 weeks, plus extra visits as needed (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Pregnancy follow-up visits). Ultrasound is offered at 11 to 14 weeks to confirm dates and viability and check for chromosomal problems, at 18 to 22 weeks to check growth and anomalies, and at 30 to 34 weeks to check placental site when needed (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Ultrasound during pregnancy). Blood pressure and urine protein are checked at every routine visit because high blood pressure after 20 weeks with protein suggests pre-eclampsia (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.24 to 1.2.28). Rhesus D-negative women can form antibodies against a rhesus-positive baby; anti-D immunoglobulin given in pregnancy and after birth prevents this (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.16; Rhophylac label, Section 1.1). Women from some ethnic groups and deprived areas have higher maternal and perinatal death rates in UK reports, so they may need closer monitoring; Saudi equivalents were not found (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.3).
keyMechanisms: Antenatal care detects problems that cause harm to mother and baby when found late, mainly pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, anaemia, infection and poor fetal growth, so that treatment or a change of care place can start early (NICE NG201, Section 1.2 Routine antenatal clinical care).

The Saudi Ministry of Health schedule sets eight timed visits, six in primary care and two in hospital after transfer at 36 weeks, plus extra visits as needed (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Pregnancy follow-up visits).

Ultrasound is offered at 11 to 14 weeks to confirm dates and viability and check for chromosomal problems, at 18 to 22 weeks to check growth and anomalies, and at 30 to 34 weeks to check placental site when needed (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Ultrasound during pregnancy).
Blood pressure and urine protein are checked at every routine visit because high blood pressure after 20 weeks with protein suggests pre-eclampsia (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.24 to 1.2.28).

Rhesus D-negative women can form antibodies against a rhesus-positive baby; anti-D immunoglobulin given in pregnancy and after birth prevents this (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.16; Rhophylac label, Section 1.1).

Women from some ethnic groups and deprived areas have higher maternal and perinatal death rates in UK reports, so they may need closer monitoring; Saudi equivalents were not found (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.3).

symptoms: Missed period and positive pregnancy test; nausea, breast tenderness, tiredness (NICE NG201, Section 1.1 Antenatal care).
At booking: concerns about nausea and vomiting, bleeding, pain, mood or domestic safety (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.1 and Recommendation 1.2.5).
Later: headache, visual disturbance, upper abdominal pain, swelling, reduced baby movements, bleeding, leaking fluid (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.3.13 and Section 1.2.26 to 1.2.34).
Mood changes, anxiety or low mood (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.1).
physicalSigns: Blood pressure, weight and body mass index at booking; blood pressure and urine dipstick at every visit (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.12, 1.2.24 and 1.2.28).
Symphysis fundal height after 24 weeks, plotted on a growth chart, no more than every 2 weeks (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.30).
Fetal movements and heart beat as appropriate (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.3.13).
Ankle swelling is common and not by itself a sign of disease (clinical judgment).
redFlags: First blood pressure 140/90 mmHg or higher after 20 weeks: refer to secondary care to be seen within 24 hours (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.26).
Blood pressure 160/110 mmHg or higher: same-day referral (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.27).

Vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, reduced or absent baby movements, rupture of membranes, fever or severe headache with visual symptoms: same-day assessment in hospital (NICE NG201, Section 1.3 and Recommendation 1.3.13).
Domestic abuse disclosed: follow the safeguarding pathway and offer a private conversation (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.5).
Previous or current severe mental illness, suicidal thoughts or psychosis: urgent perinatal mental health referral (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.1; NICE CG192).

Any condition that makes the pregnancy high risk (previous stillbirth, caesarean section, hypertension, diabetes, twins, placenta praevia): move out of the basic care pathway to specialist antenatal care (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Overview).
precipitants: Age 40 or older; first pregnancy; interval between pregnancies over 10 years; body mass index 35 or more; family history of pre-eclampsia; multiple pregnancy (NICE NG133, Recommendation 1.1.3).
Previous hypertension in pregnancy, kidney disease, lupus or antiphospholipid syndrome, diabetes, chronic hypertension (NICE NG133, Recommendation 1.1.2).
Smoking, alcohol, drug misuse (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.4 and 1.3.10).
Late booking, which may reveal social, mental health or medical problems (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.1.12).
Domestic abuse, poor social support (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.5).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Bleeding or pain in early pregnancy: arrange an early scan to confirm the pregnancy is in the womb with a heart beat (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Ultrasound during pregnancy).
Persistent vomiting with weight loss, dehydration and ketonuria rather than ordinary morning sickness (NICE NG201, Section on nausea and vomiting).
High blood pressure before 20 weeks or before pregnancy, needing specialist review (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.25).
Known diabetes or very high glucose at booking is pre-existing diabetes and needs specialist care (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.21).

differentials.condition: Iron deficiency anaemia versus haemoglobinopathy trait
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Microcytosis with low ferritin versus microcytosis with normal ferritin that needs haemoglobinopathy testing (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.13).
Mild breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness without alarm features (clinical judgment).

clinicalManagement.title: Book and see the woman early
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as pregnancy is known; before 12 weeks
actions: Book an appointment at the nearest primary care centre as soon as the pregnancy is known (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Overview).
If she books late, ask the reason because it may reveal medical, social or psychological problems (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.1.12).
Offer early advice on stopping smoking, alcohol and folic acid before the booking visit (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.1.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Take history and examine at the booking visit
actions: Ask about medical, obstetric and family history, mental health, medicines (including over-the-counter and herbal), allergies, occupation, support, smoking, alcohol and drugs (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.1).
Ask about domestic abuse when she is alone (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.5).
Measure height, weight and body mass index and blood pressure (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.12 and 1.2.24).
Assess risk of venous thromboembolism, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia and fetal growth restriction (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.18 to 1.2.29).

clinicalManagement.title: Offer booking tests and the first scan
actions: Offer full blood count, blood group, rhesus D status, HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and haemoglobinopathy screening; she can accept or decline any part (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.12 and 1.2.13).
Arrange the first ultrasound scan at 11 to 14 weeks to confirm dates and the number of babies (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Ultrasound during pregnancy).
Decide with the woman about screening for chromosomal conditions (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.14).

clinicalManagement.title: Start supplements and aspirin where indicated
actions: Advise 400 micrograms of folic acid daily up to 12 weeks, and 5 mg for those at higher risk (NICE NG247, Recommendations 1.1.4 and 1.1.5).
If at risk of pre-eclampsia, prescribe aspirin 75 to 150 mg daily from 12 weeks until birth (NICE NG133, Recommendations 1.1.2 and 1.1.3).
Check vitamin D and other vitamin advice (NICE NG247, Section on vitamin D and other vitamin supplements).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow the visit schedule
actions: Visits at 18, 24, 28, 32 and 36 weeks; the last two visits at 38 and 40 weeks are in hospital after transfer at 36 weeks (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Pregnancy follow-up visits).
At each visit measure blood pressure, test urine for protein, ask about baby movements after 24 weeks and measure fundal height (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.24, 1.2.28 and 1.2.30).
Second scan at 18 to 22 weeks; third scan at 30 to 34 weeks when indicated (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Ultrasound during pregnancy).
Glucose tolerance test at 24 to 28 weeks if at risk (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.22).
At 28 weeks repeat blood count, group and antibodies, and offer anti-D if rhesus D negative (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.16).
Discuss birth preferences before 28 weeks and labour, feeding and postnatal care after 28 weeks (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.3.14 and 1.3.15).

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate when risk appears
actions: Hypertension after 20 weeks: refer to be seen within 24 hours; 160/110 or more: same day (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.26 and 1.2.27).
Any unexpected test result: refer according to local pathways with information and support (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.17).
Change to specialist care for a pregnancy with a risk factor (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Overview).

regimens.indication: Prevention of neural tube defects in a routine pregnancy
regimens.patientGroup: All women planning pregnancy or in the first 12 weeks
regimens.dose: 400 micrograms once daily. Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, once daily, with or without food (NICE NG247, Recommendation 1.1.4)
regimens.duration: Ideally from 3 months before pregnancy, or as soon as pregnancy is known, until at least 12 weeks (NICE NG247, Recommendations 1.1.2 and 1.1.4)
adjustments: Body mass index 25 or more and increased pre-eclampsia risk: no need for more than 400 micrograms unless a high-risk factor applies (NICE NG247, Recommendations 1.1.6 and 1.1.7).
After bariatric surgery: refer for individual advice (NICE NG247, Recommendation 1.1.8).
Folic acid supplement is advised even if food is fortified (NICE NG247, Recommendation 1.1.3).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Ask about adherence and barriers at each early visit (NICE NG247, Recommendation 1.1.9).
Vitamin B12 status in anyone with anaemia or long-term vegetarian diet (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.3).
contraindications: Untreated vitamin B12 deficiency (including untreated pernicious anaemia): long-term folate therapy is contraindicated (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.3).
Not for use alone in undiagnosed megaloblastic or macrocytic anaemia (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.1).
regimens.useWhen: Routine dose for every woman; preferred unless a high-risk factor is present.
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG247: Maternal and child nutrition (2025)
regimens.sourceEdition: NICE NG247, Section 1.1 Folic acid before and during pregnancy, Recommendation 1.1.4; Folic Acid 5 mg SmPC, Section 4.3

regimens.indication: Prevention of neural tube defects in a pregnancy at increased risk
regimens.patientGroup: Women with diabetes, sickle cell disease or thalassaemia, a previous baby with a neural tube defect, or on anti-epileptic or HIV medicines
regimens.dose: 5 mg once daily. Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, once daily (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.2)
regimens.duration: Before conception and through the first 12 weeks (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.2; NICE NG247, Recommendation 1.1.5)
adjustments: In established folate deficiency in pregnancy: 5 mg daily continued to term (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.2).
Contains lactose and sucrose (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 2).
Anti-epileptic medicines (phenytoin, primidone, phenobarbital) interact with folate; seek specialist advice (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.5).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Adherence, and the neural tube check at the anomaly scan (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.15).
Vitamin B12 status if long-term use (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.3).
contraindications: Untreated vitamin B12 deficiency, including untreated pernicious anaemia and lifelong vegetarians (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.3).
Malignant disease unless megaloblastic anaemia from folate deficiency is a major complication (Folic Acid 5 mg label, Section 4.3).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when one of the NICE high-risk factors is present; start before conception if planned.
regimens.sourceTitle: Folic Acid Tablets BP 5 mg: summary of product characteristics (emc)
regimens.sourceEdition: NICE NG247, Section 1.1 Folic acid before and during pregnancy, Recommendation 1.1.5; Folic Acid 5 mg SmPC, Section 4.2 and Section 4.3

regimens.indication: Reduce the risk of pre-eclampsia in women at high or moderate-plus risk (off-label)
regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant women from 12 weeks with the risk factors in NICE NG133
regimens.dose: 75 mg to 150 mg once daily (one 75 mg gastro-resistant tablet or two for 150 mg). Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, swallowed whole with water; do not cut, chew or crush the tablet (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.2)
regimens.duration: From 12 weeks until the birth of the baby (NICE NG133, Recommendations 1.1.2 and 1.1.3)
adjustments: Off-label use: the 75 mg tablet is licensed for cardiovascular disease, and it must be prescribed for this use (NICE NG133, Section 1.1).

Doses above 100 mg per day are contraindicated in the third trimester by the SmPC; doses up to 100 mg daily need strict obstetric monitoring (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.6); NICE advises 75 to 150 mg, so decide the dose with the obstetric team.
From the 20th week prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors can cause oligohydramnios; keep the dose low (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.6).
Hepatic and renal: avoid in severe impairment (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure and urine protein at every visit (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.24 and 1.2.28).
Bleeding, peptic ulcer symptoms and allergy (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.4 and Section 4.8).
Fetal growth by fundal height and scans (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.29 and 1.2.30).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to salicylates or to prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors, including asthma triggered by them (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.3).
Active or recurrent peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; haemorrhagic diathesis or coagulation disorder (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.3).
Severe renal, hepatic or heart failure; doses above 100 mg a day in the third trimester (Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.3).
regimens.branch: Aspirin for women at risk of pre-eclampsia
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG133: Hypertension in pregnancy: diagnosis and management
regimens.sourceEdition: NICE NG133, Section 1.1 Recommendations 1.1.2 and 1.1.3; Aspirin 75 mg SmPC, Section 4.2, Section 4.3 and Section 4.6

regimens.indication: Routine antepartum suppression of rhesus D sensitisation
regimens.patientGroup: Rhesus D-negative pregnant women not already sensitised
regimens.dose: 300 micrograms (1,500 IU) as a single dose at 28 to 30 weeks; a second 300 microgram dose within 72 hours of birth if the baby is rhesus D positive or unknown; 300 micrograms within 72 hours of a sensitising event; more for a large fetomaternal bleed. 1 microgram equals 5 IU: do not confuse the units. Dilution and preparation: none; use the prefilled syringe as supplied; bring to room temperature, inspect for particles, do not freeze, single use.
regimens.route: Intramuscular or intravenous injection; if intramuscular and more than 5 mL, divide the dose between sites; never subcutaneous; observe for at least 20 minutes (Rhophylac label, Section 2)
regimens.frequency: Once at 28 to 30 weeks, once after birth, and after each sensitising event
adjustments: NICE offers it at the 28-week visit; the label regimen of one 300 microgram dose at 28 to 30 weeks is used here (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.16; Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).
Do not give live virus vaccines within 3 months (Rhophylac label, Section 7.1).
Interference with laboratory tests: passive anti-D may show on later antibody screens (Rhophylac label, Section 5.2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for 20 minutes after the injection for hypersensitivity (Rhophylac label, Section 2).
Fetomaternal haemorrhage test after a sensitising event (Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).
Cord blood group of the baby to decide on the postpartum dose (Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).
contraindications: Anaphylactic or severe systemic reaction to human immune globulin (Rhophylac label, Section 4).
IgA deficiency with IgA antibodies and a past reaction to Rhophylac (Rhophylac label, Section 4).
Not for the newborn of a mother who received it postpartum (Rhophylac label, Section 4).

branches.label: Folic acid in early pregnancy
branches.entryCriteria: Any pregnant woman before 12 weeks, or one planning pregnancy; use the higher dose when she has a risk of a baby with a neural tube defect such as previous affected pregnancy, diabetes, sickle cell or thalassaemia, or takes anti-epileptic or HIV medicines.

branches.label: Aspirin for women at risk of pre-eclampsia
branches.entryCriteria: Pregnant woman at 12 weeks or more with one high-risk factor (previous hypertensive disease, kidney disease, autoimmune disease, diabetes, chronic hypertension) or more than one moderate risk factor, with no aspirin allergy, no active ulcer and no bleeding disorder.

branches.label: Anti-D prophylaxis for rhesus D-negative women
branches.entryCriteria: Rhesus D-negative pregnant woman who has not formed anti-D antibodies, at 28 to 30 weeks, or within 72 hours of a sensitising event, with no history of severe reaction to immunoglobulin.

medicationPlan.note: Which women need which medicine follows NICE NG247, NICE NG133 and NICE NG201; doses, administration and contraindications come from the NICE text and the product labels named in each row. All doses are for adults. diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Before 12 weeks of pregnancy (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Pregnancy follow-up visits).

Eight visits: before 12 weeks, 18, 24, 28, 32, 36, 38 and 40 weeks; the first six in primary care, the last two in hospital after transfer at 36 weeks (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Pregnancy follow-up visits).
11 to 14 weeks, 18 to 22 weeks, and 30 to 34 weeks when indicated, for example to locate the placenta (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Ultrasound during pregnancy).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Eligible for the basic care component
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: A pregnant woman with no risk factor is followed in primary care; a woman with a risk factor is referred (Saudi MOH Health Care During Pregnancy page, Overview and Pregnancy follow-up visits).
One high-risk factor or more than one moderate risk factor: advise aspirin 75 to 150 mg daily from 12 weeks until birth (NICE NG133, Recommendations 1.1.2 and 1.1.3).
Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg or higher first noted after 20 weeks: be seen within 24 hours; 160/110 mmHg or higher: same day (NICE NG201, Recommendations 1.2.26 and 1.2.27).
Rhesus D-negative woman not known to be sensitised: offer at 28 weeks (NICE NG201, Recommendation 1.2.16; Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).

teaching.scope: Pregnant woman at low risk attending a Saudi Ministry of Health primary health care centre: booking visit by 12 weeks, history, examination and booking tests, the eight-visit schedule (six in primary care and two in hospital), the three ultrasound scans, screening for gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, anaemia and infection, supplements, aspirin and anti-D prophylaxis, health education and when to move her to higher-risk care. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health antenatal page for the visit and scan schedule and NICE NG201 for the content of each visit, with medicine doses, administration and contraindications from product labels and NICE guidance.
learningObjectives: Book before 12 weeks and follow the eight-visit schedule.
Check blood pressure and urine protein at every visit.
Offer the booking blood tests and three scans at the right weeks.
Give folic acid, aspirin and anti-D to the women who need them.
pitfalls: Missing a first blood pressure rise after 20 weeks.
Giving only one folic acid dose to everyone.
Forgetting rhesus status at the booking visit.
Not asking about domestic abuse when the woman is alone.
Late referral of a woman with a new risk factor.
keyPoints: Blood pressure 140/90 or higher after 20 weeks needs review within 24 hours.
Folic acid is 400 micrograms for most and 5 mg for those at higher risk.
Aspirin starts at 12 weeks and continues until birth in women at risk of pre-eclampsia.
Anti-D is for rhesus D-negative women at 28 to 30 weeks and after sensitising events.

patientEducation: Come to the clinic as soon as you know you are pregnant, ideally before 12 weeks.
Take folic acid every day until 12 weeks.
You will have blood tests and three scans; you can decline any test.
Tell us at once if you have bleeding, severe headache, blurred vision, pain under the ribs, fluid leaking or fewer baby movements.
Do not smoke or drink alcohol; check with us before any medicine or herbal product.
lifestyleAndDiet: Eat a balanced diet and drink enough water.
Avoid smoking, shisha, alcohol and recreational drugs.
Take iron and vitamin D if advised.
Plan the place of birth with your doctor.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician or family physician; midwife or nurse; obstetrician and gynaecologist; sonographer; laboratory team; dietitian; mental health professional; social worker; pharmacist.
dischargeCriteria: Booking history, examination and tests done; scan dates booked; supplements and aspirin started where indicated; rhesus status known and anti-D arranged if needed; warning signs explained; next visit date booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Visits at 18, 24, 28, 32 and 36 weeks in primary care and 38 and 40 weeks in hospital; scans at 11 to 14, 18 to 22 and, if indicated, 30 to 34 weeks; blood pressure and urine protein at every visit; extra visits for any risk.
